fund_003:n1.prompt:
You are helping me compile the financial statements needed to kick off a 409A valuation with {{vendor}}. If you don't already know it, ask me for: (1) the company's accounting system configured as {{vendor}} and confirmation you have access via my configured credentials, and (2) the valuation date or period range the 409A valuation will use (e.g., trailing 12 months or fiscal year-to-date).

Once you have that, do the following:
1. Use {{vendor}}'s reporting tools to retrieve the Balance Sheet as of the valuation date (get_balance_sheet).
2. Use {{vendor}}'s reporting tools to retrieve the Profit & Loss statement for the relevant period (get_profit_and_loss).
3. If {{vendor}} supports it, also pull a cash-flow statement for the same period, and check whether custom reports filtered/grouped by class, location, or tag dimensions are relevant to how the business is structured (e.g., multiple entities or cost centers) — if so, pull those breakdowns too.
4. Verify the reports reconcile internally (balance sheet balances, P&L totals match summary figures) and note the currency, accounting basis (cash vs. accrual), and any custom dimensions used.
5. Save or export the Balance Sheet, P&L, and (if available) cash-flow statement in a clear, labeled format (PDF or spreadsheet) ready to hand to the 409A valuation provider.

Done looks like: you have a complete, internally consistent set of financial statements (balance sheet, P&L, and ideally cash-flow) covering the correct period, clearly labeled with company name, period, and basis of accounting.

Report back with: the period covered, the accounting basis, a summary of key totals (total assets, total revenue, net income), any discrepancies or missing data you found, and the file names/locations of the exported statements.

fund_003:n2.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the cap table snapshot needed to commission our 409A valuation. Our equity management platform is {{vendor}}. If you don't already know it, ask me for: (1) our {{vendor}} issuer/company ID, and (2) confirmation of which data room or storage location (e.g., a shared drive folder) should receive the exported files.

Using your configured credentials, connect to {{vendor}}'s programmatic API and pull:
- The full capitalization table by share class (stakeholders, share classes, securities, and vesting states)
- The list of stakeholders on the cap table
- Fair market values from any prior 409A valuations on file

If {{vendor}} exposes a GraphQL cap table query instead of REST endpoints, use that method to retrieve equivalent data. Reconcile the pulled data for internal consistency: check that total shares outstanding by class match stakeholder-level sums, flag any missing vesting schedules or unlabeled securities, and note the date of the most recent prior 409A fair market value if one exists.

Export the full cap table and transaction history to an open format (Excel or CSV) so the data is portable and not vendor-locked. Save this alongside a short summary noting: total stakeholders, total share classes, total outstanding securities (common, preferred, options, SAFEs, etc.), and any discrepancies found during reconciliation.

When done, report back to me with: the export file location(s), the summary of totals and discrepancies, the date of any prior FMV data found, and a list of any data gaps I need to resolve with our cap table admin before this snapshot can be sent to the 409A valuation provider. Do not send or share this data with any third party yourself — simply prepare it and flag it as ready for my review.

fund_003:n3.prompt:
You are helping me prepare a 409A valuation engagement request in {{vendor}} (our equity-management platform) so an authorized officer can review and submit it. I have configured credentials for {{vendor}} already set up.

Before starting, ask me for any of the following if not already known: our {{vendor}} account/company URL, the legal entity to be valued, the desired effective date for the valuation, whether this is an initial or refresh/scheduled 409A, and the name/email of the officer who must approve submission.

Actions to take:
1. Log into {{vendor}} using my configured credentials and navigate to the 409A valuation section.
2. Verify our cap table data in {{vendor}} is current (option grants, share classes, recent transactions); flag any stale or missing data you find, but do not edit cap table records yourself unless I explicitly confirm the corrections.
3. Begin the 409A engagement initiation form: select the effective date, entity, and valuation type (initial vs. refresh) per my input.
4. Fill in all required fields the form asks for (company financials snapshot, prior valuation reference if applicable, contact details) using information I provide or that is already populated in {{vendor}}.
5. Save the request as a draft — do not submit it.
6. Prepare a short summary checklist showing: form fields completed, data source confirmed as current, effective date selected, and the officer designated to approve.

Done looks like: a fully filled draft 409A engagement request sitting in {{vendor}} awaiting approval, plus my checklist summary delivered to you.

Important: You must stop for human sign-off before submitting the engagement request — do not click submit, approve, or confirm the order on my behalf. Report back with the draft status, a link or location reference to the draft in {{vendor}}, and the checklist so the designated officer can review and submit it themselves.

fund_003:n4.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the 409A valuation questionnaire that our valuation provider requires before they can establish fair market value for our stock options. Please do the following:

1. Ask me for (if not already available): our latest cap table (share classes, option pool, outstanding grants), most recent financial statements, current financial projections/forecasts, details of any recent financing rounds or term sheets, a list of potential comparable public companies or recent M&A transactions in our space, and any board minutes or documents describing liquidation preferences or special rights.
2. Locate and review our internal financial and cap-table records (spreadsheets, data room, or finance system) to extract factual data points the questionnaire typically asks for: company overview, share classes and rights, historical and projected financials, recent transactions, and use of proceeds.
3. Draft pre-filled answers for every factual/objective question in the questionnaire (e.g., share counts, dates, financing terms, financial history).
4. For judgment-based questions — such as selection of comparable companies, weighting of valuation methods, growth/discount rate assumptions, or narrative descriptions of business risk — prepare a clearly labeled draft answer with your reasoning and flag it as "needs human judgment/verification."
5. Compile everything into a single organized document or form mirroring the questionnaire's structure, with drafted answers and open flags clearly marked.
6. Do not submit the questionnaire or represent any answer as final. Present the completed draft to me, including a checklist of items needing my review or confirmation, and then stop for human sign-off.

Report back with: the completed draft questionnaire, the list of data sources used, and the specific flagged items requiring my judgment before this can be sent to the valuation firm.

fund_003:n5.prompt:
You are helping me track the status of a 409A valuation report I've commissioned through {{vendor}}, our equity-management platform, while the valuation firm completes its analysis (typically 2-3 weeks).

Context: The actual valuation work is being performed by a third-party appraisal firm and its completion timeline is entirely outside our control — this waiting period remains a human step that cannot be accelerated or operated via any interface. Your job is to prepare monitoring infrastructure and check status periodically, not to wait synchronously.

Please do the following:
1. Ask me for my {{vendor}} issuer ID (or confirm you can find it from previously configured account context) if not already known.
2. Using my configured credentials, check {{vendor}}'s fair market values data for our issuer (the equivalent of retrieving the issuer's completed 409A valuation record) to see if a completed valuation is now present.
3. If no completed valuation exists yet, report that the report is still pending and note today's date so we can track elapsed time against the 2-3 week estimate.
4. If a completed valuation is found, extract and report the fair market value figure(s), the effective date, and any expiration/refresh date for the valuation.
5. Set up or note a simple reminder cadence (e.g., every 3-4 business days) for me to re-run this check until a report appears, since this cannot be fully automated end-to-end.

Done looks like: either (a) a clear status update confirming no valuation is available yet, with the date logged, or (b) confirmation that the valuation is complete along with the extracted fair market value and effective date.

Report back to me with: current status (pending/complete), any retrieved valuation data, and your suggested date for the next check-in.

fund_003:n6.prompt:
You are helping me prepare for the review and acceptance of our completed 409A valuation report before it is formally adopted by the board. Please do the following:

1. Ask me for: (a) the location of the delivered 409A valuation report (PDF or link from the valuation provider, e.g. emailed file or provider portal), (b) our company domain/entity name, (c) the effective date of the valuation, and (d) whether we use Carta or another cap table platform to house the valuation.

2. Read through the valuation report and produce a plain-language summary covering: the determined fair market value (FMV) per common share, the valuation methodology used, the effective date, the valuation firm's name, and any notable assumptions, risks, or caveats the report flags (e.g. discounts for lack of marketability, comparable company set, changes since prior valuation).

3. Cross-check the FMV against our current 409A (if one exists) and note the percentage change and how many months remain before this valuation expires or a triggering event (financing, tender offer) would require a refresh.

4. Draft a short board resolution/consent memo recommending formal adoption of this valuation as the new strike price basis, including the FMV, effective date, and valuation firm, ready for board review.

5. If we use Carta or a similar platform, prepare (but do not submit) the steps needed to upload/link the valuation report and log the FMV once approved.

6. Compile a checklist: report reviewed, summary prepared, comparison to prior valuation done, draft board resolution ready, platform upload steps documented.

Report back with the FMV summary, the comparison analysis, the draft resolution text, and the checklist. Because accepting this valuation establishes the IRS safe-harbor strike price and must be formally ratified by an authorized officer or the board, do not click accept, approve, or adopt the valuation in any system yourself — stop for human sign-off once your preparation is complete.
